description: The live-verified surface of parser refusals and tolerances. A refused statement reads 'SQL compilation error:' followed by one line per error - 'syntax error line L at position P unexpected TOK.' with the token echoed VERBATIM including case, '<EOF>' at end of input, positions 0-based on their line - and an unterminated literal instead reads 'parse error line L at position P near <EOF>.' positioned at the END of the input. A trailing comma is TOLERATED in the select list and the FROM list (and inside a CTE subquery, and after a star) and REFUSED in GROUP BY, ORDER BY, function arguments and INSERT column lists. GROUP BY, HAVING and WHERE all work without a FROM, while QUALIFY without a window function and CONNECT BY without a FROM each have their own sentence. A statement that RUNS OUT of input names '<EOF>' at the very end of the text, never at the clause keyword that started the unfinished part; trailing JUNK after an already-complete statement names the junk token instead; and a construct-leading keyword written where a column was meant is reported ONCE, at the token the construct could not swallow. Where the two parsers' error POINTS differ - the embedded one keeps a bare identifier viable as a statement start, so a leading typo fails one token later - only the shape is pinned, exactly as the Java did. Converted 1:1 from parser/SyntaxErrorShapeTest (now retired).
